rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists threatened the Prophet with their deities’ wrath for preaching monotheism; God alone can protect and sustain him, and nothing harms without His permission.
rows.anchor: These verses sound assurance to the Prophet Muh@ammad (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing harm independent of God’s permission implies that God is insufficient to protect and sustain a person, which is disbelief and polytheism.
rows.anchor: this obviously is disbelief and polytheism.

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God guides or misguides people rebukes the polytheists’ ignorance.
rows.anchor: express rebuke on the ignorance of the polytheists.

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s established practice leads these people astray because of their deeds, so none can guide them; this reassures the Prophet not to heed arrogant opponents.
rows.anchor: God has led them astray and those who are led astray by God can be guided by none.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzīz means powerful: if God were not sufficient for His servants, He would not be powerful, and one who is not powerful cannot be God.
rows.anchor: the fact is that He is زیِزَعٌ and he who is not زیِزَعٌ cannot be God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhī intiqām means that God does not spare those who violate His rights or forgive excesses against His servants, but exacts retribution for everything.
rows.anchor: He does not spare those who violate His rights nor forgives those who commit excesses against His servants

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question invokes God’s obvious, essential attributes; since He is powerful and just, His servants should fully trust Him.
rows.anchor: The above words are in the form of a question because they refer to obvious attributes of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists contradict themselves: they affirm God as creator yet assign partners to Him, treating Him as no longer master and controller of creation.
rows.anchor: in their view, God is the creator but He is not the master and controller of the world He has created.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to ask whether their alleged deities could protect him from harm God intends or prevent a blessing God grants; they cannot.
rows.anchor: can their alleged deities protect him; similarly, if God wants to bless him with some favour can these idols made of stones stop God from this.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this context, afaraʾaytum expresses the speaker’s disgust and wonder.
rows.anchor: when it occurs in the given context it signifies disgust and wonder on the part of the speaker.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet fears and hopes in no one but God, who looks after all his needs; those who trust God rely on Him, while trust in others will fail.
rows.anchor: neither does he fear anyone other than God nor does he have hope from anyone other than God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ʿalā makānatikum is elided after innī ʿāmil to avoid repetition.
rows.anchor: The words   ىَلَع ِتَانَكَمي are suppressed after  يِّنِإِ لٌِامَع to avoid repetition.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet declares his separation from the disbelievers: if they persist in their attitude, he will persist in preaching, and the future will reveal who is disgraced or destroyed and who is saved.
rows.anchor: The Almighty has asked the Prophet (sws) to declare his acquittal from the disbelievers in these verses.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future will show who succeeds and remains intact, and who suffers disgrace and destruction.
rows.anchor: the future will tell who is disgraced who is successful; who is destroyed forever and who is kept intact by God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment is called disgraceful as retribution for the opponents’ arrogance.
rows.anchor: The punishment is qualified by the word “disgraceful” because it is in retribution to the arrogance of the opponents.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdhāb muqīm refers to a punishment that takes root in a nation and ravages it completely.
rows.anchor: that punishment which visits a nation in a manner that it takes root and totally ravishes it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There are transient torments that admonish like a wave and pass, and destructive torments that visit a messenger’s nation after it deliberately rejects the truth.
rows.anchor: this torment is the one which visits the nation of a messenger after it deliberately denies the truth communicated to it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revealed Book establishes truth against falsehood; guidance benefits its recipient and misguidance harms only the rejector. The Prophet’s duty is to invite, not force faith, so he can leave them to themselves.
rows.anchor: The Almighty has revealed the Book with truth to him for the guidance of people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word yatawaffā is elided after allātī lam tamut; the author supplies it in his translation.
rows.anchor: The word  اَاهَّفَوَتَی is suppressed after  يِتَّالَو ْمَل ْتُمَت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God controls life and death: He takes souls whose term is complete, while sleep and waking daily enact death and return to life for those whose term remains; life lasts only for its appointed period.
rows.anchor: When a person sleeps everyday, it is as if he is made to observe death

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first sign is that God’s control over creation, authority, life, and death means no one else has a say in where people return.
rows.anchor: when no one has any say in life and death how can someone become the person to whom people return?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From the first sign Islahi concludes that God alone is worthy of trust, and the trusting should rely on Him.
rows.anchor: trusted; it is on Him those who trust should trust.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second sign is that resurrection is not improbable: daily sleep and waking rehearse death and renewed life, as the believer’s morning supplication reflects.
rows.anchor: a person witnesses a rehearsal of life and death everyday if only he is a man of vision.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third sign is that the universe educates people in Qur’anic truths on which their success and salvation depend.
rows.anchor: the best place for the education of facts on which rests a person’s success and salvation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question expresses wonder and rebuke that people set up intercessors besides God despite clear facts, expecting them to protect against God’s seizure.
rows.anchor: This question expresses wonder and rebuke: have these naïve people set up intercessors for themselves besides God in spite of these clear facts

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one but God has authority, and idols have no power or knowledge that could qualify them as intercessors or add anything to God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: here too no one has the ability to add to God’s knowledge in any matter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercession belongs wholly to God and requires His permission; only those permitted may speak, and their words will be wholly true, with no lying before God.
rows.anchor: intercession totally rests in the hands of God; without his permission no one will dare intercede for someone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an sets out the conditions for intercession in several places; this verse presents them comprehensively.
rows.anchor: conditions on intercession have been imposed by the Qur’an at various places
